reflections.title: "Partakers of the Divine Nature"

reflect.text: Trying to handle life on our own strength is exhausting, like walking up a steep hill against gravity. Yet the Lord has already given us everything we need for daily life and godliness through a real, personal relationship with Jesus. When fear and worry tempt us to doubt, we can remember his past faithfulness. God provides for our physical needs and gives us supernatural power to turn away from sin and live for him.

To enjoy this strength, we need to fix our thoughts on God's great promises. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, "if you will tread them the juice will flow." More than looking at the size of the gift, we look to the Promiser himself. God never changes, he cannot lie, and he has all wisdom and power. Because ignorance leads to ungodly living, we must fill our minds with deep Bible truth and talk about it with other believers.

Through these promises, God makes us partakers of his divine nature. We do not become God, but by the Holy Spirit we are joined to Christ and become like him in love, truth, and goodness. Because we belong to Jesus, we leave behind secret sins like pride and laziness, showing his holiness in our daily walk.

questions: In what areas of your daily routine are you trying to rely on your own strength instead of resting in God's promises?
How can spending time meditating on God's character help you turn away from sinful habits?
reflections.prayer: Lord, thank you for giving us everything we need for life and for following you. Help us to rest in your unfailing promises rather than trusting in our own strength. Teach us to reflect your love, truth, and purity in our daily lives. Amen.

D9.author: Hannah Benson
D9.work: Equipped for Today: What "Life and Godliness" Really Means

reflections.title: Making Your Calling Sure

reflect.text: A saving faith in Jesus is the starting point of Christian life, but God calls us to build upon it with steady effort. We are told to add courage, knowledge of Scripture, self-control, patience under trials, godliness, and love for others. When we actively pursue these qualities, our inner life grows rich and deep. As Charles Spurgeon observed, "for real usefulness, graces are better than gifts." Good fruit is simply the overflow of a heart filled with God's grace.

Practicing these virtues also brings deep peace to our souls. Doubts and lukewarm living often go hand in hand, but when we give diligence to grow, we receive strong assurance of our calling. We learn to live in God's presence and face hardship without complaining, knowing our faith is being refined like gold.

F. B. Meyer reminds us that a ship can limp into harbor waterlogged, or glide in smoothly with every sail set. Peter encourages us to live in such a way that we receive a rich, choral welcome into Christ's eternal kingdom. When we faithfully cultivate this choir of Christian graces, we will not stumble, and our lives will bring lasting blessing to others.

questions: Which of the Christian virtues mentioned in this passage do you need to cultivate most right now?
How does growing in godly character strengthen your assurance of belonging to Christ?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, give us the diligence to add courage, patience, and love to our faith. Keep us from being lukewarm or idle in our walk with you. Lead us each day so that our lives bear fruit and honor our Savior, Jesus Christ. Amen.
